value.title: Blueprint 004: procedures
value.summary: How PRD 005 is built: a `pij/procedure` ddoc in one folder per procedure, a TypeScript runner in the pij skill reached through `just proc` and `pij proc`, per-checkout progress, a drift check in harness checks, and the first procedures.

sections.name: overview
sections.value: A procedure is a folder: its ddoc, its rendering (the human how-to), and anything only it uses, including its own justfile. A project's procedures live in `docs/project/procedures/<area>/`; those that ship to every project live in `skills/pij/procedures/<area>/`. One runner, `skills/pij/tools/procedures/procedures.ts`, reads the documents and runs steps as `just` recipes, checking inputs, order and preconditions first and a done check after, and records progress in a git-ignored file per checkout. It also books ids through `pij claim`, lists procedures, records status changes through ddocs, and holds the drift check that harness checks runs. It adds no loop, poll, timer or hook: it runs only when a seat or the gate calls it.

value.name: Procedure schema
value.responsibility: The `pij/procedure` ddoc: meta (id, title, area, kind, status, owner, superseded_by), who_when, inputs, preconditions, steps (run, decision or guide; pre, requires, done, done_when, who, changes_access, proven_in_practice), commands, done_when, known_limits, mistakes, carries_out (a PRD row link plus the sentence it guarantees, required), operates (a component link, sentence optional), uses and side_effects (paths outside the folder), comments and changelog. Step `requires` is a ddocs link to another procedure's step, so ddocs checks it resolves. The skill copy must match byte for byte (pij-skill-check).

value.name: Folder layout and homes
value.responsibility: One folder per procedure holding `procedure.dd.json`, its rendering `procedure.dd.md` (the human how-to), and anything only it uses: its own `justfile`, step scripts, step tests, fixtures and templates. A project's procedures live in `docs/project/procedures`, or the home its `.pij-procedures.json` names; those that ship to every project live in the skill. In pij's repo an area lives in one home; elsewhere a project's procedure hides the skill's with the same id. `.pij-procedures.json` may also list legacy pages, which the check lets shrink but never grow.

value.name: Booking and the scaffold
value.responsibility: `proc new <area> <slug> --title <t> [--kind] [--skill]` refuses on main or in the main checkout, books the next number with `pij claim procedure-<area> --for <slug>` (one ledger, a number per area, never reused), refuses if a folder already holds that number or above, writes a valid procedure document (and a justfile for a runnable one), stages them, runs ddocs validate and build from the repo root, and prints the worktree and path it wrote.

value.name: Step runner
value.responsibility: Runs one step: gathers its inputs (`--arg name=value`, or `PROC_IN_<NAME>` from the environment; a secret input is refused on the command line), checks order (each earlier step is recorded done, or its done check passes now), checks `requires` against the other procedure's done check (live state) before its recorded progress, runs the procedure's and the step's preconditions, skips a step whose done check already passes (unless `--again`), runs the step's recipe, then requires its done check to pass before recording it. Recipes resolve in the procedure's own justfile, else the repo's root justfile, and run as `just --justfile <file> --working-directory <repo root>` with `just` found on PATH in-process and started directly. Decision steps refuse until `--decided-by` records them; guide steps point at a procedure or a page and finish with `--done` or when the procedure they follow is done. `commands` (serve, watch) run without touching progress. Unknown flags refuse; every flag reaches the step.

value.name: Run progress
value.where: <git common dir>/pij-procedures/progress.json (shared by every worktree of the clone; `.pij/procedures/progress.json` under the root only outside git)
value.responsibility: Per clone, keyed by procedure id and run key (`default` when none is given): each step's state (ran, found done, decided, marked), when and by whom. Every worktree of the clone reads and writes the same file, so a recorded decision outlives the worktree it was made in. Written with a temporary file and a rename. `--clear` empties one key. Never committed.

value.name: Entry points
value.responsibility: `just proc …` in pij (through nice19.sh) and `pij proc …` anywhere pij is installed. The shim loads the runner in-process with `require`, so `pij proc` starts no second node. Both work from any directory in a checkout: the runner finds the repo root itself.

value.name: Generated list
value.responsibility: Lists every procedure in both homes with id, title, kind, status and owner, from the files; `--json` for agents. Running a procedure with no step lists its steps as done, next or to do from progress alone.

value.name: Status changes
value.responsibility: `proc status <draft|current|superseded|retired> <proc>… --approved-by <who> [--why] [--superseded-by <id>]` sets each procedure's status and adds a changelog row naming the approver, through ddocs. Status gates nothing: a draft runs like a current procedure.

value.name: Drift check
value.where: procedures.ts (`proc check`); `just procedures-check`; harness checks stage `procedures`; `just self-check`
value.responsibility: Fails when: a procedure document sits outside a `PROC-*` folder or a folder holds other than one; the id, area or folder disagree; an area is in both homes; a step id is not four digits; a step names a recipe that neither its justfile nor the root justfile has; a guide step's target or a `requires` step is missing; a `changes_access` step has no done check; a path the folder's files or steps use outside the folder is not in `uses` or `side_effects`; a file in a procedure folder holds a relayed pij message; or a page under docs/how, docs/project or the community references has three or more numbered items that each begin with a command and no `not-a-procedure` reason. ddocs-check validates the documents and their renderings (it gains the skill home).

value.name: Reports
value.responsibility: Run only when asked: files outside a procedure's folder that only that procedure uses (with the folder each belongs in), and blueprint components of kind verb, endpoint or hook that no procedure operates.

value.name: Meta procedures
value.responsibility: PROC-meta-0001 (write a procedure) and PROC-meta-0002 (set up procedures in a repo, with the schema and the setup recipes in its folder).

value.name: Project-doc procedures
value.responsibility: Write a PRD, a blueprint and a workstream, and fold in a ruling, as PROC-docs procedures; the old community pages point at them.

value.name: pij's first procedures
value.responsibility: Change a live seat's reasoning effort, bounce the daemon after an rs merge, and take a Copilot or OMP update.

value.name: Existing how-tos sorted
value.responsibility: Every page's fate (becomes a procedure, stays as reference, deleted) is listed in workshop 003 input 003; reference pages that number commands carry a `not-a-procedure` reason.

value.name: The rule in the skill
value.where: skills/pij/SKILL.md (invariant 13, the pij proc line, an alias row); templates/roles/coder/v5 and reviewer/v4 (pinned in crates/daemon/src/community/templates.rs); AGENTS.md
value.responsibility: Find the procedure and follow it, or write one as you go: in the skill, the worker and reviewer packets, and AGENTS.md, which keeps one line per rule that moved into a procedure.

value.decision: The runner is one TypeScript file in the skill, run by node's type stripping, with no build and no dependencies.
value.why: It then works in any repo where pij is installed, as pr-freeze does, and needs no daemon or Rust change. The shim can load it in-process.

value.decision: No import line in the root justfile: the runner runs each procedure's own justfile directly.
value.why: The survey's name clashes and swallowed flags came from area modules sharing the root namespace; this removes both and keeps deleting the folder a complete removal.

value.decision: Numbers are booked with the existing claim kinds `procedure-<area>`.
value.why: `pij claim` already takes any lowercase kind with one ledger and never reuses a number, and #342 finds folders in any case. Per-area numbers give the ids the PRD names (PROC-meta-0001). The runner guards the one gap: a folder that already holds the number.

value.decision: Preconditions and done checks are recipes: exit 0 passes. Order checks run the other step's done check first and use recorded progress only when it has none.
value.why: Recipes are what seats already run, so no predicate language is needed (non-goal n-1), and live state is right when the other step ran in another checkout (osk-central's review).

value.decision: A decision step refuses until recorded; nothing waits.
value.why: Waiting needs a poll or a hook, which req-28 forbids.

value.decision: Listing never runs a check; it reads progress.
value.why: Listing is the most frequent call; it must cost nothing (req-28).

value.decision: Co-location is a report, not a gate.
value.why: The operator's ruling of 2026-11-24: a file used by one procedure today may be shared tomorrow.

value.decision: In pij's repo an area lives in one home; in another project, its own procedure hides the skill's with the same id.
value.why: Every project books its own numbers. In pij both homes share one tree, so a collision there is a mistake; elsewhere a project that already had PROC-meta-0001 (osk-central) must keep its ids, so its own wins (osk-central prime's review of #343).

value.rate: on demand only: 1 `just` per precondition, 1 done check before, 1 run, 1 done check after, plus 1 per earlier step with no recorded progress and 1 per `requires` with a done check; each `just` runs its recipe through its shell
value.scaling: with the steps a seat runs; none per seat or per tick; the daemon's spawn counter does not move

value.what: Listing procedures or a run's progress.
value.scaling: with the number of procedure files

value.rate: 1 `git ls-files` and 1 `just --summary` per justfile (the root and each procedure's), per run of the gate; no build, no network
value.scaling: with procedures that have a justfile

value.rate: no launch beyond the shim's own node (the runner is loaded in-process)
on demand: one `pij claim` request (the daemon scans in-process), a few git calls, and ddocs validate, set and build per document
